stemMd: A study reports a positive correlation between two measured variables. What does this statement alone imply?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Higher values of one tend to occur with higher values of the other.

options.label: B
options.textMd: No third variable can influence them.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Every individual observation lies exactly on a straight line.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Changing the first must cause the second to change.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The two variables have identical numerical values.

explanationMd: Positive correlation describes the direction of association in the data. It does not by itself establish a causal mechanism, exact equality, or absence of other influences.

distractorRationale.c: Positive correlation need not be perfect.
distractorRationale.d: Association alone does not establish causation.
